llm_text: The table outlines recommended system requirements for running ECMiner, including CPU type, memory capacity, operating system version, and hard drive space needed. Each row represents a specific requirement with corresponding minimum specifications listed in the right column. Roles: Rows represent different hardware/software components needed, while columns indicate the required minimum values for each component.
table_html:
[PRECEDING_TEXT] Recommended System Requirements [TABLE_HTML]
CPU Intel® Core i5 or higher
Memory 16 Gbytes or more
Operating System Windows 10 or higher
Hard Disk space 3.5 Gbytes + Free space at least 2x the amount of data to be analyzed

llm_text: This table describes various windows and their functions in ECMiner, categorized by number and window name. Each row explains a specific window's role, such as managing nodes, displaying resources, workspace usage, property details, error logs, and help documentation. Rows represent numbered windows, while columns detail the window's name, description, and function. The table provides comprehensive information on how different parts of the software interface serve distinct purposes.
table_html:
[TABLE_HTML]
Num. Window name Description
(1) Menu Creating/editing/saving project and files
(2) Node Node for ‘Data’, ‘Chart’, “Modeling’, ‘Output’ and ‘Model Evaluation’. Data loading (data input), data manipulation to filter, derive variables and define indep. & dep. variables.
(3) ResourceWindow Resource Menu The resource window displays with Local, Model, and Output. Local displays the list of the current working folder. Model stores the current data analytical node. Output stores the results of executing the current project.
(4) ResourceList The window displays the contents of the selected menu (Local, Model, Output) in the Resource menu.
(5) Workspace Working space for data handling and model configuration
(6) Node Property Information for data and model specification and output at each node
(7) Message Log messages about errors and process information
(8) Dynamic Help The help for the node properties

llm_text: The ECMiner manual notes that the output from the Display Node is best saved as a data file (.ecl) rather than an output file (.ept), due to how the data is generated; users need to manually save the output using the Display Node's save function.
table_html:
[TABLE_HTML]
NOTE Since the output of the Display Node is generated as data, it should be saved as a data file(*.ecl) rather than as an output file (*.ept). Therefore, you must use the save button within the Display Node screen to save the output. [image:rId121]

llm_text: This table outlines options for configuring the ECMiner software, detailing how users can customize date/time formats, treat numerical data as floats, filter file types, adjust the program's appearance, and set floating-point number display formats. Each row represents a specific configuration option, while columns provide details about what each setting does. Roles: - Rows represent different configuration options available in the software. - Columns explain the purpose and functionality of each option.
table_html:
[TABLE_HTML]
Num. description
(1) You select the date/time display format based on the language.
(2) Choose this option if you want to treat all numerical data as floating-point numbers when reading data.
(3) Specify the types of files to be displayed in the Resource window. Enter the file extensions you want to display, separated by ";". Extensions like ecm, ecl, ept, gms, etc., are selected by default even if not specified.
(4) Specify the overall look of the program. Set it to a form that is visually pleasing to the user.
(5) Specify the display format for floating-point numbers when presenting data on screen or in reports.

Rows represent configuration options, while columns indicate details about each option including a number and description.
table_html:
[TABLE_HTML]
Num. description
(1) Enter the database connection information for nodes related to OLE DB.
(2) Enter the database connection information for nodes related to ODBC.
(3) Selecting this option will automatically fill in the database connection information when adding nodes related to the database.

Rows represent different actions or states related to managing the most-used nodes list, while columns provide details about each step's purpose and function.
table_html:
[TABLE_HTML]
Num. description
(1) All nodes supported by ECMiner™ are listed.
(2) (1) is used to add the selected node to "Most used nodes".
(3) To remove a node from "Most used nodes," select the node to be removed at (4) and press this button.
(4) This is the current list of nodes added to "Most used nodes."
